body_fields.rule: Text an app paints on a canvas is byte-equal across hosts only with its glyph origins on whole device pixels, so a canvas shot holding such text is held to one cross-OS digest only when painted so.
body_fields.why: The CPU renderer snaps glyph origins differently on Apple hosts.
body_fields.because: A canvas shot holding app-painted text now stands in the cross-OS digest table, byte-equal only by the whole-pixel snap, a limit stated on a delegate's word that no standing row holds and the cross-OS shot exception has no room to take.

body_fields.name: Widget click point read against the content box
body_fields.rule: An app that places custom-widget content from a click point reads that point against the widget's content box, subtracting border and padding from the element's client rect.
body_fields.why: A widget paints in its content box while an element's client rect is its border box.
body_fields.because: The chunk measured that a click point read against the client rect lands off by the border and padding, a rule for every app painting from a click that the content-box paint row has no room to hold.

body_fields.name: Canvas placement only at the click centre
body_fields.rule: A driver click lands at the centre of its target element, so an agent places content on a canvas only at the canvas's centre, no verb landing a pointer elsewhere.
body_fields.why: Stated as a measured limit of the driver where an agent reads it.
body_fields.because: The capability statement gains the limit that an agent places canvas content only at the centre, on a delegate's word, a limit the click contract's centre landing does not state.

body_fields.capability: A keyboard path into a custom-widget canvas: the Circle Drawer canvas is reached by pointer alone
body_fields.because: The chunk builds the canvas with no keyboard path into it, a whole capability the project does not have.

body_fields.name: Canvas text glyph origins on whole device pixels
body_fields.rule: Text an app paints on a canvas is byte-equal across hosts only with each glyph origin on a whole device pixel, so canvas text checked by digest across hosts is drawn with its glyph origins so placed.
body_fields.why: The CPU renderer snaps glyph origins on Apple hosts to a different grid than elsewhere.
body_fields.because: The chunk's fix found canvas text differing on macOS and made the label byte-equal on all three hosts by whole-pixel glyph origins, a rule future canvas text must follow, applied ahead of ratification.

body_fields.name: Click synthesis on a custom-widget element
body_fields.rule: On a custom-widget element the engine delivers every pointer event to the widget first, then synthesises the app's click on the main button, context menu on the secondary button and double click on a second click within the window, with no click walk and no focus clear.
body_fields.why: So an app's onclick and ondoubleclick on a widget element fire for every app behind custom-widget; upstream's widget arm returned before the synthesis.
body_fields.because: The chunk changed the engine so a widget element's click and double-click handlers fire, a decision every Dioxus native app behind custom-widget now relies on.

body_fields.name: Circle Drawer circles painted on one canvas
body_fields.rule: Circle Drawer's drawing area is one canvas element of role group named Drawing area, keyed and lint clean at boot; its circles are carried by one data-circles attribute, x,y,d per circle joined by semicolons with malformed text read as no circle, and are painted, never DOM nodes.
body_fields.because: The chunk replaced the circle DOM nodes with one painted canvas element, so circles now cross as shot pixels alone, a decision applied ahead of ratification.

body_fields.promise: A widget paints in its element's content box while the element's client rect is its border box, so an app placing widget content from a click point subtracts the element's border and padding.
body_fields.because: The chunk measured the widget paint box against the click point and Circle Drawer now subtracts its border, a promise every app placing widget content relies on.

body_fields.why: The canvas paints from widget code, not the cascade; an exception to colours living in stylesheets.
body_fields.because: The chunk moved the circle colours out of CSS into the widget, a hardcoded exception the palette must record.

The engine now synthesizes the UA click on a custom-widget target: behind the custom-widget feature, after the widget's own handle_event and the focus set, a pointerdown is recorded, a pointerup yields Click on the main button or ContextMenu on the secondary, and a Click with a count of two queues DoubleClick, with no click walk and no focus clear; an app's onclick and ondoubleclick on a widget element now fire, the widget still hearing every pointer event first (the founder's word, F2; upstreamable, not sent).
The stand sample's Circle Drawer replaced its div canvas and its circle DOM nodes with one object element, role group, named Drawing area, keyed circle-canvas, painted by a custom widget from Rust that reads a data-circles attribute (x,y,d triples, semicolon-joined; malformed text read as no circle, no panic) and paints each circle and its diameter as canvas text, the scene clipped to the paint box.
Circles leave the DOM, snapshot, tree, graph and lint and cross only as shot pixels; no verb, argument, carrier, field, refusal cause, session error, exit code, log field or span was added.
The sample crate gained four workspace-inherited dependencies (anyrender, blitz-dom, parley, peniko), no new package in the lock; build, audit (advisories ok, licenses ok) and the fast leg green.
After implement the diameter label is drawn with its glyph origins on whole device pixels, so the canvas shot is byte-equal on linux, windows and macOS; the capability statement gained Circle Drawer, the click on a widget element and two stated limits (a click lands at an element's centre; canvas text across hosts).
The circle-drawer answers F3 to F5, data-circles, the fourth dependency, the glyph snap and the stated limit are the escher overseer's word, PROVISIONAL; F1 and F2 are the founder's.
